\begin{theorem}[Deterministic time is contained in space]
\lean{Complexity.DTIME_subset_SPACE}
\label{Complexity.DTIME_subset_SPACE}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.DTIME, Complexity.DTIME_eq_empty_of_exists_zero, Complexity.SPACE, Turing.MultiTapeTM.initCfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM.spaceUsed, Turing.MultiTapeTM.spaceUsed_le_mul_succ}
\difficulty{4}
For every time bound $T : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$, every language decidable in
deterministic time bounded by a constant multiple of $T$ is decidable using space
bounded by a constant multiple of $T$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Polynomial time uses polynomial space]
\lean{Complexity.P_subset_PSPACE}
\label{Complexity.P_subset_PSPACE}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.DTIME_subset_SPACE, Complexity.P, Complexity.PSPACE}
\difficulty{1}
Every binary language decidable in polynomial time is decidable using polynomial space;
equivalently, $\mathsf{P} \subseteq \mathsf{PSPACE}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Clean simulation with bounded head positions]
\lean{Complexity.b2b_clean_run}
\label{Complexity.b2b_clean_run}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.cleanTM, Complexity.LogProg.cleanTM_run, Turing.Cfg.init, Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime, Turing.FinTM.computesInTime_iff, Turing.MultiTapeTM.initCfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.spaceUsed, Turing.MultiTapeTM.spaceUsedByTape_le_spaceUsed}
\difficulty{3}
Let $M$ be a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, and suppose it computes
$y$ from $x$ in $t$ steps using at most $s$ work-tape cells. The clean simulation of
$M$, started in its initialization state on $x$, has some run time $T$ at which it is
halted, its output is $y$, every work-tape cell is blank, and every work-tape head is at
the origin. At every time from $0$ through $T$, each work-tape head lies within distance
$s$ of the origin.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Polynomial-time clean verifier]
\lean{Complexity.b2b_clean_verifier}
\label{Complexity.b2b_clean_verifier}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.CleanRun, Complexity.LogProg.cleanTM, Complexity.P, Complexity.P_subset_PSPACE, Complexity.b2b_clean_run, Turing.FinTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.indicator}
\difficulty{3}
Let $V$ be a language of Boolean words in polynomial time. Then there are natural
numbers $e,c_V$ and a finite Boolean Turing machine $M_V$ such that, for every Boolean
word $y$, the clean simulation of $M_V$ started in its initialization state on $y$ halts
with output consisting of the single indicator bit of whether $y$ belongs to $V$. At its
halting time all work-tape cells are blank and all work-tape heads are at the origin;
throughout the run, every head position has absolute value at most $c_V(|y|^e+1)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Rewind machine states]
\lean{Complexity.B2bRewindState}
\label{Complexity.B2bRewindState}
\leanok
Introduce a finite state type with three states: `start`, `scan`, and `done`.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Input rewind machine]
\lean{Complexity.b2b_rewindTM}
\label{Complexity.b2b_rewindTM}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.B2bRewindState, Turing.FinTM.controlAction, Turing.MultiTapeTM}
For each natural number $k$, define a $k$-work-tape Boolean Turing machine whose initial
state is `start`. From `start` it moves the input head one position left and enters
`scan`; in `scan` it moves left and remains there when the scanned input symbol is
Boolean, and moves right and halts when the scanned cell is blank. In `done` it stays in
that state without moving the input head; these transitions make no work-tape changes
and emit no output.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Rewind run reaches the left boundary]
\lean{Complexity.b2b_rewind_run}
\label{Complexity.b2b_rewind_run}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.B2bRewindState, Complexity.b2b_rewindTM, Turing.Cfg, Turing.FinTM.rewind_heads, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom}
\difficulty{3}
Let $k\in\mathbb{N}$, let $x$ be a Boolean word, and let $c$ be a configuration of the
rewind machine on $x$ whose state is the start state. There is a natural number $r\le
c$'s input-head position $+2$ such that after $r$ steps the machine is halted at
input-head position $1$, with all other configuration fields unchanged from $c$;
throughout those $r$ steps, every work-tape head position is unchanged.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Rewind of the virtual host]
\lean{Complexity.b2b_vhost_rewind}
\label{Complexity.b2b_vhost_rewind}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.B2bRewindState, Complexity.b2b_rewindTM, Complexity.b2b_rewind_run, Turing.Cfg, Turing.FinTM.VirtualTag, Turing.FinTM.bufferTape, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.vhostBuffer, Turing.vhostCfg, Turing.vhostEmitTM, Turing.vhostEmitTM_runFrom}
\difficulty{4}
Let $x,y$ be Boolean words, let $c$ be a configuration of the rewind machine on input
$y$ with state start, let $b$ be a Boolean boundary tag satisfying the virtual-head
boundary condition for $c$'s input-head position, let $p$ be a valid input-head position
for input $x$, and let $\mathrm{pre}$ be a Boolean word. There exist a natural number
$u\le c$'s input-head position $+2$ and a Boolean tag $b'$ such that after $u$ steps of
the virtual-host simulation of the zero-work-tape rewind machine, the configuration is
the virtual host of $c$ with halting state and input-head position $1$, tag $b'$,
position $p$, and output prefix $\mathrm{pre}$; its buffer head is at the origin and its
buffer tape stores $y$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Verdict machine states]
\lean{Complexity.B2bVerdictState}
\label{Complexity.B2bVerdictState}
\leanok
Introduce a finite state type with states `left`, `read`, and `done(b)` for each Boolean
value $b$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Boolean work tape verdict machine]
\lean{Complexity.b2b_verdictTM}
\label{Complexity.b2b_verdictTM}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.B2bVerdictState, Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.inputMoveAction, Turing.tapeAction}
For a natural number $k$ and a selected work tape $i$ among the $k$ work tapes, define a
Turing machine with Boolean symbols and states $\text{left}$, $\text{read}$, and
$\text{done}(b)$ for $b\in\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$. Its initial state is
$\text{left}$. In state $\text{left}$ it moves the head of work tape $i$ one cell left and
enters $\text{read}$; in state $\text{read}$, if the scanned cell contains $b$, it erases
that cell and enters $\text{done}(b)$, while a blank cell leads to
$\text{done}(\mathrm{false})$ without changing the tape. In state $\text{done}(b)$ it
remains in that state without moving the input head.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Trace of the verdict machine]
\lean{Complexity.b2b_verdict_trace}
\label{Complexity.b2b_verdict_trace}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.B2bVerdictState, Complexity.b2b_verdictTM, Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.workTapeSymbols, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step', Turing.moveInputPos_zero, Turing.step_of_tapeAction_move, Turing.step_of_tapeAction_write}
\difficulty{4}
Let $k$ be a natural number, let $x$ be a Boolean word, let $i$ be one of the $k$ work
tapes, and let $d$ be a configuration of the verdict machine with state left. Suppose
the cell immediately to the left of tape $i$'s head contains the Boolean $b$. For every
natural number $t\le 2$, the configuration after $t$ steps is $d$ if $t=0$; if $t=1$,
only the state changes to read and tape $i$'s head moves left by one; and if $t=2$, the
state is done with value $b$, that cell is erased, and the head remains at the cell it
reached after the first step.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Binary Anchor Machine]
\lean{Complexity.b2b_anchorTM}
\label{Complexity.b2b_anchorTM}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.inputMoveAction}
For every natural number $k$, define a $k$-work-tape Turing machine over the Boolean
alphabet with a single state. Its initial state is the unique state, and every
transition uses the fixed action requesting zero movement of the input head and the
unique state as successor.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Binary Answer Machine]
\lean{Complexity.b2b_answerTM}
\label{Complexity.b2b_answerTM}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinTM.emitAction, Turing.MultiTapeTM}
For every natural number $k$ and Boolean value $b$, define a $k$-work-tape Turing
machine over the Boolean alphabet with two states, numbered $0$ and $1$. Its initial
state is $0$, and in state $q$ every transition uses the action that emits the
one-symbol word consisting of $b$ and has successor state $q$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Two-step Boolean answer]
\lean{Complexity.b2b_answer_run}
\label{Complexity.b2b_answer_run}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.b2b_answerTM, Turing.Cfg, Turing.FinTM.emit_halts, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom}
\difficulty{1}
Let $b$ be a Boolean symbol and let $c$ be a configuration of a $k$-work-tape machine
over the Boolean alphabet, on input $x$, whose state is $0$. The machine that emits $b$
and then halts reaches a halted configuration after two steps, with output equal to the
original output of $c$ followed by $b$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Hosted Source Machine]
\lean{Complexity.b2b_hostedSource}
\label{Complexity.b2b_hostedSource}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.B2bRewindState, Complexity.LogProg.CleanSt, Complexity.LogProg.cleanTM, Complexity.b2b_rewindTM, Turing.FinTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.embedEmitRetTM, Turing.seamCompTM}
Given a finite Turing machine $M$ over the Boolean alphabet, define a machine with twice
as many work tapes as $M$, over the Boolean alphabet, and with states comprising tagged
copies of the states used for the rewind, cleaning, and simulation phases. The machine
is built by composing an emitted-return rewind phase, a cleaning simulation of $M$
initialized in its initial state, and a further rewind phase, with the indicated phase
states and initial cleaning state.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Identity embedding of a configuration]
\lean{Complexity.b2b_embed_refl}
\label{Complexity.b2b_embed_refl}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.embedEmitCfg, Turing.embedEmitCfg_selected_pos, Turing.embedEmitCfg_selected_tape}
\difficulty{3}
Let $k$ be a natural number, $S$ a type, $x$ a finite Boolean input word, and $c$ a
configuration of a $k$-tape Turing machine on input $x$. For any assignment of contents
and head positions to the $k$ work tapes, embedding $c$ into the same set of tapes by
the identity embedding, with an empty output prefix, leaves $c$ unchanged.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Hosted source computation and space bound]
\lean{Complexity.b2b_hostedSource_run}
\label{Complexity.b2b_hostedSource_run}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.B2bRewindState, Complexity.LogProg.CleanRun, Complexity.LogProg.CleanSt, Complexity.LogProg.cleanTM, Complexity.b2b_embed_refl, Complexity.b2b_hostedSource, Complexity.b2b_rewindTM, Complexity.b2b_rewind_run, Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.init, Turing.Cfg.mapState, Turing.FinTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.exists_first_halt, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.visitedByTapeHead, Turing.embedEmitRetTM, Turing.embedEmitRetTM_run, Turing.seamCompTM, Turing.seamCompTM_run_ofCfg, Turing.seamCompTM_visitedByTapeHead_ofCfg}
\difficulty{6}
Let $M$ be a finite-state Boolean Turing machine with $k$ work tapes, let $y$ be a
Boolean word, let $b$ be a Boolean value, and let $B\in\mathbb{N}$. Suppose the cleaned
machine associated with $M$, started in its prescribed initialization state on input
$y$, halts with output consisting of the single symbol $b$, leaves every work-tape cell
blank and every work-tape head at position $0$, and keeps every work-tape head within
distance $B$ of $0$ at every step up to halting. Then, from the hosted machine's initial
configuration on $y$ with any valid input-head position among the $|y|+2$ positions, the
hosted machine reaches a configuration with no state and output $[b]$ in finitely many
steps; at every step up to and including that time, each work-tape head remains within
distance $B$ of $0$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Binary value of a string of ones]
\lean{Complexity.b2b_counter_value}
\label{Complexity.b2b_counter_value}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
For every natural number $Q$, the base-two value of the length-$Q$ digit string

\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Orbit of fixed-width binary increment]
\lean{Complexity.b2b_certificate_orbit}
\label{Complexity.b2b_certificate_orbit}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Meyer.enumWord_zero, Complexity.Meyer.incFixed_enumWord, Complexity.enumWord, Turing.incFixed}
\difficulty{4}
Let $Q,r$ be natural numbers with $r<2^Q$. Starting from the length-$Q$ all-zero word,
apply fixed-width little-endian binary increment $r$ times, treating overflow as leaving
the word unchanged. The resulting word is the length-$Q$ little-endian binary
representation of $r$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Bounded-witness characterization]
\lean{Complexity.b2b_verifies_iff}
\label{Complexity.b2b_verifies_iff}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Meyer.ctrVal_lt, Complexity.Meyer.enumWord_ctrVal, Complexity.Meyer.length_enumWord, Complexity.TimeHierarchy.ctrVal, Complexity.enumWord}
\difficulty{4}
Let $x$ be a Boolean word, let $V$ be a language of Boolean words, and let $Q$ be a
natural number. There is an integer $r$ with $0\le r\le 2^Q-1$ such that appending the
width-$Q$ little-endian binary word of $r$ to $x$ gives a word in $V$ if and only if
there is a Boolean word $u$ of length $Q$ such that appending $u$ to $x$ gives a word in
$V$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Concatenation of buffered words]
\lean{Complexity.b2b_buffer_concat}
\label{Complexity.b2b_buffer_concat}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinTM.bufferTape}
\difficulty{5}
For Boolean words $x$ and $u$, place the buffered copy of $u$, shifted to begin at cell
$|x|$, on the cells from $|x|$ through $|x|+|u|-1$, and use the buffered copy of $x$
elsewhere. The resulting tape content is exactly the buffer storing the concatenated
word $x u$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Polynomial-space membership from a ledger bound]
\lean{Complexity.b2b_mem_PSPACE_of_ledger}
\label{Complexity.b2b_mem_PSPACE_of_ledger}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.PSPACE, Complexity.SPACE, Complexity.SPACE.mono_const, Complexity.space_poly_subset_PSPACE, Complexity.succ_pow_le, Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime, Turing.MultiTapeTM.indicator, Turing.MultiTapeTM.initCfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM.spaceUsed}
\difficulty{4}
Let $L$ be a language of Boolean words, let $M$ be a finite Turing machine over the
Boolean alphabet, and let $D,f\in\mathbb{N}$. Suppose that for every Boolean word $x$,
there is a time $t$ at which $M$ halts with output consisting of the single Boolean
indicator of whether $x\in L$, and uses at most $D(|x|+1)^f$ work-tape cells. Then $L$
belongs to polynomial space.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Tape count formula]
\lean{Complexity.b2b_tapeCount}
\label{Complexity.b2b_tapeCount}
\leanok
For natural numbers $v$, $i$, and $p$, define the tape count to be $3+2v+2i+2p$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Index of a Word Tape]
\lean{Complexity.b2b_wordTape}
\label{Complexity.b2b_wordTape}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.b2b_tapeCount}
For natural numbers $v$, $i$, and $p$, and an index $j$ with $0 \le j < 3$, define the
corresponding word-tape index to be $j$ in the set of tape indices
$\{0,1,\ldots,2v+2i+2p+2\}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Offset Bank Embedding]
\lean{Complexity.b2b_bankEmb}
\label{Complexity.b2b_bankEmb}
\leanok
Let $off$, $m$, and $K$ be natural numbers with $off+m\le K$. Define an injective map
from the indices $0,\ldots,m-1$ to $0,\ldots,K-1$ by sending each index $j$ to $off+j$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Call Tape Embedding]
\lean{Complexity.b2b_callEmb}
\label{Complexity.b2b_callEmb}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.b2b_tapeCount}
For natural numbers $v$, $i$, and $p$, define an injective map from the indices
$0,\ldots,2v$ to the tape indices $0,\ldots,3+2v+2i+2p-1$. It sends $0$ to $1$ and each
positive index $j$ to $j+2$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Singleton Tape Embedding]
\lean{Complexity.b2b_singleEmb}
\label{Complexity.b2b_singleEmb}
\leanok
For a natural number $K$ and an index $i\in\{0,\ldots,K-1\}$, define an injective map
from the singleton index set to the $K$ indices by sending its unique element to $i$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Test-machine phases]
\lean{Complexity.B2bTestPhase}
\label{Complexity.B2bTestPhase}
\leanok
A test-machine phase is one of six labels: anchor, identity, rewind, copy, call, or
verdict.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Phase-indexed test states]
\lean{Complexity.b2b_testState}
\label{Complexity.b2b_testState}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.B2bRewindState, Complexity.B2bTestPhase, Complexity.B2bVerdictState, Complexity.LogProg.CleanSt, Turing.FinTM, Turing.SweepPhase}
Given two finite Turing machines $M_V$ and $M_I$ over the Boolean alphabet, associate a
state type to each test-machine phase. The anchor phase has a singleton state type;
identity has the cleaning states for $M_I$ together with a singleton alternative; rewind
has the rewind states together with a singleton alternative; copy has the three sweep
phases; call has a singleton alternative together with a Boolean paired with a choice
among the rewind states, a singleton alternative, the cleaning states for $M_V$ together
with a singleton alternative, and another copy of the rewind states; verdict has the
verdict states.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Test-phase machines]
\lean{Complexity.b2b_testPhases}
\label{Complexity.b2b_testPhases}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.B2bTestPhase, Complexity.LogProg.cleanTM, Complexity.b2b_anchorTM, Complexity.b2b_bankEmb, Complexity.b2b_callEmb, Complexity.b2b_hostedSource, Complexity.b2b_rewindTM, Complexity.b2b_tapeCount, Complexity.b2b_testState, Complexity.b2b_verdictTM, Complexity.b2b_wordTape, Turing.FinTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.copyTM, Turing.embedEmitRetTM, Turing.embedSilentRetTM, Turing.vhostEmitTM}
Given three finite Turing machines $M_V$, $M_I$, and $M_P$ over the Boolean alphabet,
associate a multi-tape Turing machine to each test-machine phase. Each machine has
$3+2k_V+2k_I+2k_P$ work tapes, where $k_V,k_I,k_P$ are the respective work-tape counts,
and uses the phase-indexed test states for $M_V$ and $M_I$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Test-phase redirects]
\lean{Complexity.b2b_testRedirect}
\label{Complexity.b2b_testRedirect}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.B2bTestPhase, Complexity.b2b_testState, Turing.FinTM}
Given finite Turing machines $M_V$ and $M_I$ over the Boolean alphabet, define a partial
redirect from a test phase and a state of that phase to a phase-state pair. Every anchor
state redirects to the identity phase in its initial cleaning state for $M_I$; an
identity singleton state redirects to rewind-start; a rewind singleton state redirects
to the copy sweep state; the copy done state redirects to call with its initial rewind
state and Boolean value true; and a call singleton state redirects to verdict-left. All
other phase-state pairs have no redirect.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Test-machine host]
\lean{Complexity.b2b_testTM}
\label{Complexity.b2b_testTM}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.b2b_tapeCount, Complexity.b2b_testPhases, Complexity.b2b_testRedirect, Complexity.b2b_testState, Turing.FinTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.phaseHostTM}
Given three finite Turing machines $M_V$, $M_I$, and $M_P$ over the Boolean alphabet,
the test-machine host is a multi-tape Turing machine with $3+2k_V+2k_I+2k_P$ work tapes
and states consisting of a test phase paired with a state for that phase. Its initial
state is the anchor phase with its unique state; its phase machines are the test-phase
machines, and transitions between phases follow the test-phase redirects.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Body-machine phases]
\lean{Complexity.B2bBodyPhase}
\label{Complexity.B2bBodyPhase}
\leanok
A body-machine phase is one of three labels: test, clear, or increment.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Phase-indexed body states]
\lean{Complexity.b2b_bodyState}
\label{Complexity.b2b_bodyState}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.B2bBodyPhase, Complexity.b2b_testState, Turing.FinTM, Turing.FlagPhase, Turing.SweepPhase}
Given finite Turing machines $M_V$ and $M_I$ over the Boolean alphabet, associate a
state type to each body-machine phase: the test phase uses a test-machine phase paired
with a state for that phase, the clear phase uses the three sweep phases, and the
increment phase uses a run phase, a Boolean-indexed rewind phase, or a Boolean-indexed
done phase.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Body-phase machines]
\lean{Complexity.b2b_bodyPhases}
\label{Complexity.b2b_bodyPhases}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.B2bBodyPhase, Complexity.b2b_bodyState, Complexity.b2b_tapeCount, Complexity.b2b_testTM, Complexity.b2b_wordTape, Turing.FinTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.clearTM, Turing.incrementTM}
Given three finite Turing machines $M_V$, $M_I$, and $M_P$ over the Boolean alphabet,
associate a multi-tape Turing machine to each body-machine phase, with
$3+2k_V+2k_I+2k_P$ work tapes and the corresponding phase-indexed body states. The test
phase uses the test-machine host, the clear phase clears the word on the second work
tape, and the increment phase increments the word on the first work tape.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Body phase redirects]
\lean{Complexity.b2b_bodyRedirect}
\label{Complexity.b2b_bodyRedirect}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.B2bBodyPhase, Complexity.b2b_bodyState, Turing.FinTM}
Given Boolean-alphabet machines $M_V$ and $M_I$, define a phase transition map on the
body phases test, clear, and increment. It sends the test phase's false-verdict exit to
the clear phase's sweep state, the clear phase's exit to the increment phase's run
state, and the increment phase's true-verdict exit to the test phase's anchor state;
every other phase-state pair has no redirect.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Body machine construction]
\lean{Complexity.b2b_bodyTM}
\label{Complexity.b2b_bodyTM}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.b2b_bodyPhases, Complexity.b2b_bodyRedirect, Complexity.b2b_bodyState, Complexity.b2b_tapeCount, Turing.FinTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.phaseHostTM}
Given Boolean-alphabet machines $M_V$, $M_I$, and $M_P$, define a machine with
$3+2k_V+2k_I+2k_P$ work tapes, where $k_V,k_I,k_P$ are their respective numbers of work
tapes. Its states are indexed by a body phase—test, clear, or increment—and a state for
that phase; it is the phase-host machine formed from the body phases associated with
these three machines, starting in the test phase at its anchor and using the body
redirects.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Host phase labels]
\lean{Complexity.B2bHostPhase}
\label{Complexity.B2bHostPhase}
\leanok
Define the host phases to be setup, origin, counter, zero, rewind, loop, and last,
together with answer phases indexed by a Boolean value.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Host phase state spaces]
\lean{Complexity.b2b_hostState}
\label{Complexity.b2b_hostState}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.B2bHostPhase, Complexity.B2bRewindState, Complexity.LogProg.CleanSt, Complexity.b2b_bodyState, Complexity.b2b_testState, Turing.CounterLoopState, Turing.FinTM, Turing.FlagPhase, Turing.SweepPhase}
Given Boolean-alphabet machines $M_V$, $M_I$, and $M_P$, assign a state space to each
host phase as follows: setup uses the cleaned-state space for $M_P$ together with a unit
state; origin uses a rewind state paired with a Boolean, or a unit state; counter uses
the sweep phases; zero uses the flag phases; rewind uses a rewind state or a unit state;
loop uses the counter-loop states over the body states; and last uses the test states.
Each answer phase uses a two-element state space.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Machines for host phases]
\lean{Complexity.b2b_hostPhases}
\label{Complexity.b2b_hostPhases}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.B2bHostPhase, Complexity.LogProg.cleanTM, Complexity.b2b_answerTM, Complexity.b2b_bankEmb, Complexity.b2b_bodyTM, Complexity.b2b_hostState, Complexity.b2b_rewindTM, Complexity.b2b_singleEmb, Complexity.b2b_tapeCount, Complexity.b2b_testTM, Complexity.b2b_wordTape, Turing.FinTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.copyTM, Turing.counterLoopTM, Turing.embedEmitRetTM, Turing.embedEmitTM, Turing.embedSilentRetTM, Turing.incrementTM, Turing.vhostEmitTM}
Given Boolean-alphabet machines $M_V$, $M_I$, and $M_P$, define for each host phase a
multi-tape machine with the state space assigned to that phase and with
$3+2k_V+2k_I+2k_P+1$ work tapes. The phase machines perform, respectively, cleanup
setup, origin marking, counter copying, incrementing, rewinding, the counter loop
running the body machine, a final test, or the answer procedure; the designated tape
embeddings and the Boolean answer parameter are those specified by the corresponding
phase.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Host phase redirects]
\lean{Complexity.b2b_hostRedirect}
\label{Complexity.b2b_hostRedirect}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.B2bHostPhase, Complexity.b2b_hostState, Turing.FinTM}
Given Boolean-alphabet machines $M_V$, $M_I$, and $M_P$, define a redirect map between
host phase states as follows: the setup exit goes to the origin phase at its start state
with flag true; the origin exit goes to the counter sweep; the counter exit goes to the
zero phase's run state; the zero phase's false-flag exit goes to the rewind start; and
the rewind exit goes to the loop's decrement run state. The loop's completed state
redirects to the last phase's test anchor, while its escape state goes to the true
answer phase; the last phase's verdict exit goes to the answer phase carrying that
verdict. All other phase-state pairs have no redirect.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Host machine construction]
\lean{Complexity.b2b_host}
\label{Complexity.b2b_host}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.b2b_hostPhases, Complexity.b2b_hostRedirect, Complexity.b2b_hostState, Complexity.b2b_tapeCount, Turing.FinTM, Turing.phaseHostTM}
Given Boolean-alphabet machines $M_V$, $M_I$, and $M_P$, define a Boolean-alphabet
finite Turing machine with $3+2k_V+2k_I+2k_P+1$ work tapes, where each $k$ is the
corresponding machine's number of work tapes. Its state is a host phase together with a
state for that phase; it is the phase-host machine formed from the host phase machines,
starting in setup at the cleanup initialization state for $M_P$'s initial state and
using the host phase redirects.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Polynomial ledger bound]
\lean{Complexity.b2b_ledger_bound}
\label{Complexity.b2b_ledger_bound}
\leanok
\difficulty{6}
For all natural numbers $C,c,c_V,e,c_I,c_P,K$, there are natural numbers $D,f$ such
that, for every $n\in\mathbb{N}$,
$K\bigl(2(n+C(n+1)^c+c_V((n+C(n+1)^c)^e+1)+c_I+c_P(n+1)+1)+1\bigr)\le D(n+1)^f$.
\end{theorem}

outside the image of $\iota$. Let $x,y$ be Boolean words, let $p$ be an input-head
position for $x$, and let $s$ be a state of $M$. Suppose the tape contents on every
embedded tape are blank at every cell. Embedding the initial configuration with state
$s$, input-head position $p$, and output $y$ into the larger machine gives the initial
configuration with the same state and input-head position, with $y$ buffered on tape
$\mathrm{cap}$, that tape's head at position $|y|$, and every other tape and head as
specified by the original tape contents and zero head positions.
\end{theorem}

of work tapes. Let $k$ be a natural number, let $\iota$ be an injection from the $2m$
tapes of the cleaning machine for $M$ into $k$ tapes, and choose a tape $c$ among those
$k$ tapes that is not in the image of $\iota$. For any background tape contents and head
positions, and any Boolean words $x,y$ and natural numbers $t,s$, suppose $M$ halts with
output $y$ on input $x$ after $t$ steps and uses at most $s$ cells of work-tape space
through that time. Then there are a natural number $T$ and an input-head position $p$
such that the return machine, started with the cleaning machine’s initial configuration
embedded through $\iota$ and the reserved tape initialized to capture its output,
reaches at time $T$ the configuration with input-head position $p$, output $y$, and
return state. At every earlier time it is not in the return state; at every time through
$T$ it is not halted and its output is empty. Throughout those times the head on tape
$c$ lies between $0$ and $|y|$, inclusive; every tape in the image of $\iota$ has its
head within distance $s$ of the origin; and every other tape head remains at its
prescribed background position.

Let $M_V$, $M_I$, and $M_P$ be finite-state Boolean-input Turing machines, let $x,u$ be
Boolean words, let $b$ be a Boolean, and let $t_i,s_i,s_v$ be natural numbers. Suppose
$M_I$ halts on input $x$ after $t_i$ steps with output $x$ and uses at most $s_i$ cells
of space, and the cleaned simulation of $M_V$ on input $x\mathbin{+\!\!+}u$ halts with
output $b$, clears all work tapes, returns all work heads to the origin, and keeps every
work head within distance $s_v$ of the origin. Starting the associated trial machine in
its anchor phase with input head at position $1$, buffer $u$, and the other designated
tapes blank, there is a positive time $T$ at which it is in the verdict state recording
$b$, with the buffer still $u$ and the copied word $x\mathbin{+\!\!+}u$ in the designated
tape. At every earlier time $r$ with $0<r<T$ it is not in the anchor state, and at every
$r<T$ it is not in any verdict state; through time $T$ it never halts or emits output,
and every work-head position has absolute value at most $|x|+|u|+s_v+s_i+1$.
\end{theorem}

be Boolean words such that the fixed-width increment of $u$ is $v$ and $|v|=|u|$. Start
the associated round-body machine in its clearing phase with its first work tape storing
$u$, its second storing $x$ followed by $u$, all other tapes blank, input-head position
$1$, and the specified initial work-head positions at zero. There is a positive time $T$
at which it reaches the test-anchor configuration with first tape storing $v$, all other
tapes blank, input-head position $1$, and the specified work-head positions zero; at
every earlier time it is neither in the test-anchor state nor in the test phase's
true-verdict state. At every time through $T$, every work-tape head position has
absolute value at most $|x|+|u|+1$.
\end{theorem}

Let $M_V,M_I,M_P$ be finite Turing machines over the Boolean alphabet, let $x,u,v$ be
Boolean words, and let $b$ be a Boolean value. Suppose that $M_I$ halts on $x$ with
output $x$ after $t_I$ steps and uses at most $s_I$ work-tape cells; the cleaned
simulation of $M_V$ on the concatenation of $x$ and $u$ halts with output $[b]$, has
blank work tapes and all work-head positions zero at termination, and keeps every
work-head position within absolute value $s_V$ throughout; and the fixed-width increment
of $u$ is $v$ with $|v|=|u|$. Start the round-body machine at its test-anchor
configuration with first tape storing $u$, all other tapes blank, input-head position
$1$, and the specified work-head positions zero. There is a positive time $T$ such that,
if $b$ is true, the machine ends at the true-verdict configuration with the same first
tape and with the second tape storing $x$ followed by $u$; if $b$ is false, it ends at
the test-anchor configuration with first tape storing $v$ and all other tapes blank. At
every intermediate time $r$ with $0<r<T$, its state is neither endpoint state, and
through time $T$ every work-tape head position has absolute value at most
$|x|+|u|+s_V+s_I+1$.
\end{theorem}

associated host machine with $4+2k_V+2k_I+2k_P$ work tapes and state set $\text{Fin}(2)$,

$x$, a Boolean value $b$, and a configuration $c$ of $H$ on input $x$ whose state is
$0$, map the state of $c$ to the answer phase for $b$ and run $H$ for two steps. The
resulting configuration is halted, its output is the output of $c$ followed by $b$, and
at every time $r\leq 2$ its work-tape head positions equal those of $c$.

Let $Q,e,c_V,c_I$ be natural numbers, let $V$ be a language of Boolean words, and let
$M_V,M_I,M_P$ be finite-state Boolean Turing machines. Suppose the clean simulation of
$M_V$, started in its initial state on any Boolean word $y$, halts with output equal to
the indicator of whether $y\in V$, clears all work tapes and returns all work-tape heads
to the origin, and throughout the run keeps every work-tape head within distance
$c_V(|y|^e+1)$ of the origin. Suppose also that $M_I$ computes the identity on every
Boolean word of length $n$ in time $c_I(n+1)$, and that its space use on every input at
every time is at most $c_I$. Then, on every Boolean input $x$, the specified search
machine, started with its loop state, a false word of length $Q$ on its first work tape,
and a true word of length $Q$ on its last work tape, halts with output indicating
whether there is a word $u$ of length $Q$ such that the concatenation of $x$ and $u$
belongs to $V$. At every time up to and including that halting time, each work-tape head
stays within distance $|x|+Q+c_V((|x|+Q)^e+1)+c_I+1$ of the origin.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{4}
Let $C,c,e,c_V,c_I,c_P$ be natural numbers, let $V$ be a language of Boolean words, and
let $M_V,M_I,M_P$ be finite Boolean Turing machines. Suppose that for every word $y$,
the cleaned simulation of $M_V$ on $y$ halts with output indicating whether $y\in V$,
leaves all work tapes blank with heads at zero, and uses head positions bounded by
$c_V(|y|^e+1)$. Suppose $M_I$ computes the identity in time $c_I(n+1)$ on inputs of
length $n$ and uses at most $c_I$ space at every time on every input. Suppose $M_P$ maps
each word $x$ to a unary word of length $C(|x|+1)^c$, computes this in time
$c_P(n+1)^{c+1}$ on inputs of length $n$, and uses at most $c_P(|x|+1)$ space at every
time on input $x$. Then for every Boolean word $x$, the host machine computes the
indicator of the language of words $z$ for which there exists a word $u$ of length
$C(|z|+1)^c$ such that $z$ followed by $u$ belongs to $V$. It does so in some finite
time and uses space at most
$(K+1)\bigl(2(|x|+C(|x|+1)^c+c_V((|x|+C(|x|+1)^c)^e+1)+c_I+c_P(|x|+1)+1)+1\bigr)$, where
$K=3+2k_V+2k_I+2k_P$ and $k_V,k_I,k_P$ are the numbers of work tapes of the three
machines, respectively.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Containment of NP in polynomial space]

\uses{Complexity.NP, Complexity.PSPACE, Complexity.b2b_clean_verifier, Complexity.b2b_host, Complexity.b2b_host_contract, Complexity.b2b_ledger_bound, Complexity.b2b_mem_PSPACE_of_ledger, Complexity.b2b_tapeCount, Turing.FinTM.computesFunInTime_id_spaceUsed, Turing.FinTM.computesFunInTime_polyUnary_spaceUsed}
\difficulty{3}
Every language in $\mathrm{NP}$ belongs to $\mathrm{PSPACE}$, the class of languages
decidable using polynomial space; that is, $\mathrm{NP}\subseteq\mathrm{PSPACE}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Three-SAT belongs to polynomial space]
\lean{Complexity.SAT3_mem_PSPACE}
\label{Complexity.SAT3_mem_PSPACE}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.NP_subset_PSPACE, Complexity.PSPACE, Complexity.SAT3, Complexity.SAT3_mem_NP}
\difficulty{1}
The language of binary strings whose decoded CNF formula has at most three literals per
clause and is satisfiable is decidable by a finite Turing machine that, on every input
of length $n$, halts with the correct single-bit answer while using at most $C(n^c+1)$
work-tape cells, for some natural numbers $C$ and $c$.
\end{theorem}
